correctness.rationale: The exact 2-by-2 coupled system has Frobenius separation one and rank-one solution; Gaussian/Haar trigonometric coordinates give independent arcsine laws. The conditional tail becomes a quadratic interval of exact length sqrt(1-t)/(2R), yielding an integrable limit and an O(R^-3) endpoint remainder. The constant integral evaluates to 2 asinh(1)/pi^2; bounded error shifts preserve tails; layer cake proves iff p<1. The package verify.py checked exact identities and finite-R quadratures. No numerical sample substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Zulfiqar 2026 treats the same general Petrov–Galerkin compression, but only gives sufficient disjoint-field-of-values well-posedness rather than Haar probability tails. Beckermann–Kressner–Tobler 2013 proves positive Kronecker-operator bounds in different hypotheses; Fasi–Hashemi 2026 concerns the exact Sylvester solution. Accessible local historical claims and published semantic search hits have different projection laws or error objects. The exact coupled-gap constant and p=1 cutoff are not implied by the inspected material; uncertainty about abstract-only sources and general inverse-moment literature remains.
residual_risks: Classic general inverse-moment or random Galerkin literature could already imply this explicit two-dimensional computation even without matching keywords.
Beckermann 2011 full text and Fasi–Hashemi 2026 full text were not accessible in the available inspection; abstract-only reading cannot establish their complete noncoverage.
This model is a generic Haar trial-space benchmark, not an execution of either structured algorithm proposed by the motivating source.

value.rationale: The source makes projected solvability conditional on field-of-values separation; this benchmark proves an exact probabilistic integrability frontier even though the full operator is separated and the true solution rank one. The sharp 1/R constant, error law and moment cutoff distinguish almost-sure numerical solvability from expected-error robustness and provide a reproducible randomized trial-space risk test. It is not claimed as a general algorithmic convergence result.
